native_result.query: How is the advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students related to Socioeconomic status levels?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students is more pronounced at lower SES levels with the interaction term for Socioeconomic status and being black having a coefficient of 0.7606
native_result.HypoB: BA-completion advantage for Black students is not yet observable in this file (BA proxy = HGC 1979 >= 16; rates 0.0%/0.15%/0.60% across low/mid/high childhood-SES terciles in cohort 1, only 5 cases). The robust finding is a strong monotonic childhood-SES gradient in adjacent attainment (HS>=12: 17.1->34.0%, OR 2.59; postsec>=13: 4.2->12.6%, OR 2.47) and a racial deficit concentrated at low SES that attenuates as SES rises (HS gap -20.9 to -13.2 pp). Hypothesis: SES is the dominant moderator of the racial education gap; Black students' educational disadvantage - and any eventual BA-completion differential - is concentrated at low SES levels and attenuates with rising SES. Direct-BA component anchored on 5 cases (directional only); substantive anchor is the HS/postsec gradient.
native_result.WorkflowB: cleaning (HGC=95 invalid) -> childhood SES composite [log(income1979+1), mother HGC, father HGC], median-imputed within cohort, terciles within cohort 1 -> attainment rates by SES with Wilson CIs -> cross-cohort contrast (within-cohort terciles) -> logistic robustness (SES+sex+age) -> sensitivities (complete-case SES; adult wealth 1996)

sub_hypo.context: Students in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79), with emphasis on lower socioeconomic status levels.
variables: BA degree completion rate (no explicit column provided)
sub_hypo.relations: Socioeconomic status moderates the advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students: the advantage is more pronounced at lower SES levels. The coefficient for the interaction between socioeconomic status and being Black is 0.7606.

sub_hypo.text: Among Black students, childhood SES has a strong monotonic positive association with high-school and postsecondary attainment.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 racial/ethnic cohort 1 (Black), using attainment recorded in 1979 and within-cohort childhood-SES terciles. HGC=95 is treated as invalid; SES components are median-imputed within cohort. Robustness models adjust for sex and age, with complete-case SES and adult wealth in 1996 used in sensitivity analyses.

sub_hypo.text: Childhood SES is the dominant moderator of the racial education gap: Black students' educational disadvantage is concentrated at low SES and attenuates as SES rises.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 cross-cohort comparisons of attainment recorded in 1979, using within-cohort SES terciles. HGC=95 is invalid; SES components are median-imputed within cohort. Logistic robustness adjusts for SES, sex, and age; sensitivities use complete-case SES and adult wealth in 1996.
variables: Total net family income, previous calendar year, 1979

sub_hypo.text: A BA-completion advantage for Black students is not yet observable; any eventual BA-completion differential is hypothesized to be concentrated at low SES and attenuate with rising SES, but the direct BA evidence is directional only.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 attainment recorded in 1979, with BA completion proxied by HGC>=16 and HGC=95 excluded as invalid. Only five BA-proxy cases occur in Black cohort 1; the substantive evidence rests on HS and postsecondary attainment rather than direct BA completion.
